title: Algeria Sets Its Sights on the Sahel
gist: Foreign Policy's Africa Brief says Algeria is aggressively reclaiming its Sahel security-mediator role (fighter jets to Niger, Sonatrach drilling, Trans-Saharan pipeline, rupture with the UAE) while Morocco pushes a rival gas pipeline and Atlantic access. It also covers the Ethiopia-Eritrea escalation, a $1.5B US-Zambia health deal, Ghana's BRICS application, and Erik Prince's Vectus Global losses in Congo.

insights.claim: Algeria is intervening more readily in neighbors' affairs, sending four Su-30 jets, a refueling aircraft and a transport plane to Niger's junta in August to help thwart an internal coup attempt.
insights.speaker: Nosmot Gbadamosi
insights.so_what: Algeria projecting force in the Sahel raises its role in regional security and shifts the balance versus Russia and the UAE.
insights.locator: This shift is perhaps most evident in Niger

insights.claim: Algerian state firm Sonatrach began drilling in Niger's Kafra oil block in August, reviving a stalled project, and construction of the Trans-Saharan gas pipeline from Nigeria through Niger to Algeria's coast for export to Europe began in June.
insights.speaker: Nosmot Gbadamosi
insights.so_what: Algeria is tying security influence to energy infrastructure, supporting its role as a gas supplier to Europe.

insights.claim: Algeria reopened its airspace to Mali in July after a 15-month rift over a downed Malian drone, and may have helped persuade Tuareg rebels to withdraw from Kidal, which Mali and its Russian allies retook.
insights.speaker: Nosmot Gbadamosi
insights.so_what: Thawing Algiers-Bamako relations indicates Algerian mediation is returning after the collapse of the Algiers Accord in 2024.
insights.locator: The Malian military and its Russian allies

insights.claim: Algeria severed diplomatic ties with the UAE in September, accusing it of destabilizing the region by backing rebel factions in Sudan, Libya and the Sahel, driven by fear of being isolated by Russia and the UAE.
insights.speaker: Nosmot Gbadamosi
insights.so_what: Algeria-UAE rupture signals a deepening Gulf-vs-North Africa rivalry affecting regional investment.
insights.quote: Wherever they set foot, blood flows
insights.locator: Algiers is particularly concerned about Abu Dhabi

insights.claim: Morocco's rival strategy uses economic diplomacy, including the Nigeria-Morocco gas pipeline through 12 countries (construction expected within two years) and a Dakhla Port link for landlocked Sahelian states, to support its Western Sahara claim.
insights.speaker: Nosmot Gbadamosi
insights.so_what: Competing gas pipelines to Europe are a sign of Algeria-Morocco competition; follow execution risk.

insights.claim: Analyst Intissar Fakir cautions that Algeria's actions in the Sahel should not be read only through rivalry with Morocco because the security landscape has multiple actors.
insights.speaker: Nosmot Gbadamosi
insights.so_what: Avoid simple binary framing when assessing regional risk.
insights.quote: Morocco is not anymore the only actor involved in Sahel security

insights.claim: Ethiopia and Eritrea are trading accusations of aggression, with TPLF fighting in Tigray, raising the prospect of a wider Red Sea proxy war unless third parties intervene.
insights.speaker: Nosmot Gbadamosi
insights.so_what: Red Sea escalation risk matters for shipping and regional security.

insights.claim: Zambia signed a five-year $1.5 billion US health financing deal after rejecting a $2 billion offer in May over patient-data and specimen sharing and ties to critical minerals; the new deal decouples minerals and excludes pathogen sharing.
insights.speaker: Nosmot Gbadamosi
insights.so_what: Shows African governments are pushing back on bundling aid with mineral access.

insights.claim: Ghana applied to be a BRICS partner to diversify trade and pursue resource sovereignty, with Ghana-India trade up from $3 billion in 2024 to nearly $7 billion in 2026, and China removing tariffs on most African imports in May.
insights.speaker: Nosmot Gbadamosi
insights.so_what: Growing African alignment with BRICS partners indicates diversifying trade flows away from Western conditionalities.

insights.claim: Erik Prince's Vectus Global lost at least 20 mercenaries killed or wounded in an ambush in eastern Congo, as Congo seeks US favor under a minerals-for-security deal, and Joseph Kabila announced he would lead a new rebel coalition including M23.
insights.speaker: Nosmot Gbadamosi
insights.so_what: Security risk to eastern Congo mining operations and US-backed minerals access is rising.
